query: screening and shortlisting in recruitment process
sub: A fair, fast process in 6 steps

steps.title: Set your criteria first
points: Agree them with everyone who reviews
steps.tip: Decide what good looks like before you read a single CV.

steps.title: Build a simple scorecard
points: Note the evidence for each score
Use the same sheet for every applicant
steps.tip: A shared spreadsheet is enough. No special software needed.

steps.title: Look for potential
points: Count projects, societies and part-time jobs
Don't rule people out for a short CV
steps.tip: Most intern applicants have little experience. That is the point.

steps.title: Reduce bias
points: Hide names and photos if you can
Have two people score each application
steps.tip: Two reviewers catch what one misses.

steps.title: Add a short task
points: Link it to the real work
Give clear instructions and a deadline
steps.tip: Never use a task to get free work out of applicants.

steps.title: Close the loop
points: Offer short feedback where you can
steps.tip: A kind, quick no protects your reputation with students.

cta_sub: Save these steps for your next hiring round.

captions.linkedin:
Screening and shortlisting intern applicants: a fair, fast process.

A pile of applications and no system is where good candidates get missed. Try this:

1. Set your criteria before you read a CV
2. Build a simple 1 to 5 scorecard
3. Look for potential, not years of experience
4. Reduce bias: hide names if you can and use two reviewers
5. Add a short task linked to the real work
6. Close the loop with everyone, including the people you turn down

Save this for your next hiring round.
